column1: # P-M2c PATTERN LEDGER — opened by the E1 warm-up (READER_BRIEFING §2 / D-059.3)
# era_status vocabulary: ACTIVE | DORMANT | DEAD | REACTIVATED | MUTATED->id | HYPOTHESIS
# Every pattern names the EXACT sheet fields a strictly-causal detector would read (D-026/D-056:
# a pattern must be censusable before any feature is built from it).
# n_support / n_against count cases in the 24-case E1 warm-up draw ONLY. This is a seed, not a census.

column3: A phase that has not yet spent its expected move, with the whole session left to run, prints a phase extreme and rolls over; the phase then makes its move in the rollover direction and the session-close exit collects it.
column4: NEWS-WINDOW, OPEN-DYNAMICS, REVERSAL-CONFIRMATION (all three instances are HG/NY SHORT)
column5: S3.COVERAGE_phase <= 70% ; S9.ladder_position in {below_q10, at_or_above_q10} ; S3.runway_to_phase_close >= 26000s ; S13.exit_default = session close ; age of S3.phase H (SHORT) or L (LONG) <= 200s ; S5.mid_slope_$/min and S5.accel(1m-5m) both signed with the trade
column10: The round's principal product. All three are the ONLY phase-close certificates >= $1300 in the draw. Near-misses HG-20210929-058037-S (COVERAGE 75.6%, slope +) and HG-20210929-066533-S (COVERAGE 106.3%, slope +) paid $732.50 and $595 — the coverage and slope terms are what discriminate. NEEDS A CENSUS BEFORE ANY FEATURE.

column3: When the default exit is a PHASE close and the phase has spent most of its expected move, the certificate cannot reach the bar however good the entry is. Evaluate A1 against the exit second, not the session.
column5: S3.COVERAGE_phase >= 75% ; S3.unspent <= $450 ; S13.exit_default = phase_close (not session close) ; S3.runway_to_phase_close
column10: 5/5 sub-bar. HG-20210701-019514-L is the proof case: phase_close +$20 while peak_exit was +$1220 nine hours later, outside the exit rule.

column3: When exit_default is SESSION close, the SESSION coverage row binds, not the phase row. A phase with room inside a session at >100% coverage is not capacity.
column10: Surfaced by the ablation truncated view of NKD-20210818-055996-L, where COVERAGE_NY=26.5% and COVERAGE_SESSION=101.3% disagreed.

column3: A 60-second window with no transacting counterparty cannot carry a $1,000 move regardless of every other section. The cheapest veto in the sheet.
column5: S8.60s n and vol (== 0 or 1) ; S7.300s n_trades <= ~15 with c2f >= ~20 ; S5.trades/min z <= -1.3
column10: 4/4. Co-located with B3's cell law: all four are NKD outside Tokyo. Reads from two integers.

column3: spread_at_decision far above the asset's era-median spread is a liquidity fact, not a transient quote; the entrant pays it and the book behind it cannot carry the trade.
column5: S13.spread_at_decision vs ERA_PRIMER §2 spread_med ; S13.cost_rt ; S7.L1 sizes
column10: Both cases carried spread >= 1.5x median; both walled out. Overturns B6's "costs are small" at the tail.

column3: A multi-family level confluence (fvol ladder + PHASE_HL/PRIOR_DAY) being tested for the FIRST time (tc=1, test_m<=2) and failing is a durable entry object with a very small MAE.
column5: S4.family + level_id + price + tc <= 1 + test_m <= 2 ; distance to entry ; S3 pivot at that price within ~2 min
column10: The draw's only D-021 winner I took. A5+B2 in one object. n=1 — needs a census.

column3: Large one-sided aggressive flow that fails to move the mid is being absorbed by the passive side; the flow stream is not evidence when the price stream contradicts it.
column5: S8.60s sflow/vol >= ~0.4 ; |S5.mid(NOW) - S5.mid(T-1m)| <= 1 tick ; S7.c2f (low = real fills)
column9: NKD-20210818-027352-L(-167.50; 223 contracts at 4:1 buy moved the mid $2.50, peak_exit +$107.50)
column10: The correct counterweight to A3. Cheap: three fields.

column3: A same-price stack of prior-session / prior-phase LOW levels that price has traded BELOW becomes the densest resistance object on the sheet; identifiable mechanically by |L-family level_ids carrying POSITIVE d$.
column5: S4.level_id suffix in {|L} with d$ > 0 ; count of distinct families at one price ; S4.tc, test_m
column9: HG-20210929-013657-L(+57.50, never cleared inside the phase)
column10: n=1 and confounded with P002 on that case. Do not build a feature until censused separately.

column3: sign(S8 phase sflow) x which side of the phase volume mass the mid sits on was hypothesised to say which side is trapped and therefore which way price continues.
column5: S8.FUEL MAP above_mid / below_mid / at_mid ; S8.phase sflow
column10: Invented at NKD-20210701-007741-L and used in 9 of 24 calls. It was right only where nothing was at stake and wrong on every bar-clearing move. KILLED IN THE SAME ROUND THAT BIRTHED IT. Surviving use: degenerate-state detection (phase_total < ~50 contracts at a phase open).

column3: Fuel-map symmetry + zero sflow on every window + an S4 POC/VWAP nest at d$~0 was hypothesised to mean "no trade here".
column5: S8 |above_mid-below_mid|/phase_total < 0.05 ; S8 sflow ~ 0 on 60s/5m/30m/phase ; S4 POC or VWAP level with |d$| <= 25
column10: Dead as a VETO. A balance node with unspent phase capacity (P001) is a COIL, not an absence. MUTATED->P001: the discriminator is S3.COVERAGE_phase, not the balance itself.

column3: Two-stream agreement at magnitude is a valid REFUSAL criterion when it fails and an invalid ENTRY criterion when it holds, because it describes the next ~30 minutes and the certificate is a multi-hour walled hold.
column5: S5.sflow/min series ; S7.dBsz/min, dAsz/min ; S8.60s buy/sell_vol ; S13.exit_default horizon
column10: Directly qualifies briefing item A3. Both failures were SI, both walled, one with mae_before_peak=$0.00.

column3: S5's static bid_sz/ask_sz levels give a sign-inverted A4 read when the thin side is thin because it is being AGGRESSED, not because it is withdrawing. Only S7's rate fields and S8's through-book log disambiguate.
column5: do NOT use S5.bid_sz/ask_sz alone ; use S7.dBsz/min vs dAsz/min and S8.through_book_600s direction

column10: A sheet-reading law, not a market pattern. Directly amends briefing item A4.
